Lipa Noi is a long, quiet, very shallow beach on Samui's west coast, 6 km (10–15 minutes) south of Nathon and 30 km (40–50 minutes) from the airport. The water is calm for much of the year, including many days in the October–December monsoon, and at high tide it is ideal for toddlers; at low tide the sea retreats over wide sand flats. It faces west for some of Samui's best sunsets, and the Raja car ferry from Donsak (220 THB for a foot passenger, about 1.5 hours) lands here. Restaurants are few, and Grab is unreliable on this coast.

Map of Lipa Noi

Lipa Noi stretches along the west coast between Nathon in the north and Taling Ngam in the south. The ring road runs a little inland; lanes lead down to the beach between villas and small resorts. The Raja ferry pier is on this stretch of coast.

The beach

Lipa Noi is one of Samui's longest and least developed beaches. The sand is fine and flat, the bottom is sandy with no coral, and the sea is very shallow for a long way out. Coconut palms, villas, a few small resorts and a beach club line the shore. It feels local and residential rather than touristy, with very few sunbeds or vendors. The trade-off is that the water is never deep and clear like the east coast's coves.

Tides and swimming

Lipa Noi is a tidal beach, so plan your swim around high tide.

TideWhat the beach is likeGood for
High tideShallow, calm water close to the shore over a sandy bottomToddlers, paddling, an easy swim
Mid tideKnee- to thigh-deep for a long way outWading, children with buckets
Low tideWide wet-sand flats; the sea is far outWalking, crab-spotting, sunset reflections; not swimming

Safety at Lipa Noi

  • Monsoon: the west coast is sheltered from the north-east monsoon waves that bring red flags to Chaweng and Lamai in October–December, so Lipa Noi is often calm then. It still rains hard; November is the wettest month at about 445 mm.
  • Box jellyfish: calm, shallow, warm water after rain is the kind of condition in which jellyfish come inshore. Avoid swimming at dusk, watch children closely, and if someone is stung pour vinegar on the sting for at least 30 seconds, don't rub it, and call 1669.
  • Sun: shallow water and flat sand reflect strong sun; use shade at midday.
  • No lifeguards: shallow does not mean supervised.
  • Medical help: Koh Samui Hospital (government) on the edge of Nathon is 10–15 minutes north (+66 77 913 200); private hospitals are in the Chaweng area, 35–45 minutes away.

See Koh Samui beach safety.

Lipa Noi for families with small children

For parents of babies and toddlers, Lipa Noi is one of the best beaches on Samui: at high tide the water is shallow, warm and flat, the bottom is soft sand, and there are no waves on most days. It is also one of the few beaches that stays calm in the east-coast rough season. The downsides are few restaurants within walking distance, no shops or pharmacy on the beach, and long drives to the east-coast attractions. Families who want both calm water and more facilities often compare Lipa Noi with Choeng Mon on the north-east coast. More on Koh Samui with kids and where to stay with kids.

In short: Lipa Noi has the calmest, shallowest water and the best monsoon-season record; Choeng Mon balances calm water with facilities; Chaweng has everything nearby but rougher seas in the wet months.

Sunset at Lipa Noi

Lipa Noi faces west, so the sun sets over the sea, and at low tide the wet flats turn into a mirror. Sunset is around 17:55 in November, 18:15 in January, 18:30 from February to May and 18:40–18:45 in June and July. February–April has the clearest skies; October–December sunsets are often hidden by cloud. Other west-coast options, including Taling Ngam and the Five Islands just to the south, are on Koh Samui sunset spots.

The Raja ferry pier

Lipa Noi is where the Raja car ferry from Donsak on the mainland arrives. It is the usual route for people bringing a car or motorbike to the island.

Raja FerryDetails (2026)
RouteDonsak (Surat Thani) ↔ Lipa Noi, Koh Samui
CrossingAbout 1 hour 30 minutes
FrequencyRoughly hourly from early morning to about 19:00, with extra sailings from late December to April
Foot passenger220 THB
Cars and motorbikesCarried on the same boats; vehicle fares are not published online, so check at the port
Phone (Lipa Noi office)+66 77 423 190

Rental scooters and cars from Samui are usually not insured off the island, so check your contract before taking one on the ferry. Foot passengers usually find the Seatran ferry to Nathon more convenient, as Nathon has more taxis and songthaews. Full options are on Surat Thani to Koh Samui and how to get to Koh Samui.

Beach clubs and food

Lipa Noi has few restaurants, and most are attached to resorts. The best-known venue is Nikki Beach Koh Samui, a beach club and resort open in 2026 with its Amazing Sundays brunch (12:00–16:30) and a Friday BBQ dinner with fire show (18:00–21:00); see our Nikki Beach guide, and occasional big events such as its White Party in March. Expect beach-club prices. A few small Thai restaurants and sunset bars along the beach serve simpler food. For cheap dinners, Nathon's night food market (daily 16:30–22:00) is 10–15 minutes north. See Koh Samui beach clubs and restaurants.

Where to stay in Lipa Noi

Lipa Noi is mostly villas and small resorts. West-coast prices run from about 1,500 THB a night for a simple room to 6,000 THB and more for a pool villa. It suits families with toddlers, long stays, couples who want sunsets and quiet, and people who arrive by car on the Raja ferry. It does not suit nightlife lovers or anyone without a car or scooter: Chaweng is 35–45 minutes away, and Grab drivers are scarce. See where to stay on Koh Samui and Koh Samui villas.

Nearby places

  • Nathon, 6 km north: ferries, the night market, the old town and the government hospital.
  • Hin Lad waterfall, inland from Nathon: a steep jungle trail, about two hours return.
  • Taling Ngam, 5 km south: the Five Islands sunset and Baan Suan Lung Khai.
  • Paradise Park Farm (9.4862, 99.9833): a hilltop farm park inland, listed in October 2026 as open 09:00–17:00; we could not confirm the gate fee, so check before you go.
  • Ziplines: one zipline and ATV operator is based in the Lipa Noi hills.
  • Laem Yai, north of Nathon: a quiet sunset shore.

The Xperience art park

In the hills above Lipa Noi, The Xperience is Koh Samui's new immersive art park: 12 zones of giant sculptures, a heart-shaped lagoon beach club, pools and a projection-mapping and fire show after dark. It opens Wednesday to Sunday from 11:00 (Fridays until midnight); Day Pass tickets are 1,500 THB.

Road distances; times for normal daytime traffic. Fares are typical 2026 ranges; taxis have no meters. Grab is weak on the west coast: you can usually get a car out, but the return, especially after sunset, can take a long time or fail, so book a driver in advance. Scooter rental on the west coast is at the cheap end of the island's 150–350 THB a day range for a 125 cc. Parking at the beach lanes is free. See getting around Koh Samui.
